summary: Asymmetric refill window causing 429s for SSE sessions and delayed batch callbacks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports steady 429s affecting server-sent-events (SSE) long-lived streams and delayed/failed batch callback webhook deliveries after a recent rate-limit window tuning change on their Dedicated pool. The pattern appears tied to asymmetric refill timing between the edge (signed-url/callback) accounting path and the origin refill window used for batch token accounting.

Impact:
- EdgeScale Labs: intermittent 429s for real-time dashboards (SSE) causing UI disconnects and missed update notifications.
- Batch pipeline: callback webhooks from large backfills are delayed or returned 429s, necessitating retries and causing billing/throughput churn.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dl-prod-dedicated-03 (us-west primary, eu-west failover)
- Tokens: customer uses signed upload URLs for batch workers and persistent SSE connections for dashboards.
- Rate policy: mixed windowing (short-window=10s for realtime, refill=1s smoothing disabled for batch).

Observed behaviour:
- SSE clients receive 429s after 12-18 minutes of steady traffic, usually following a large batch callback spike.
- Batch callback requests intermittently receive 429s even after console shows available burst credits.
- Console token counters drift: edge shows earlier refill timing than origin, then reconciles after ~90s.

Expected behaviour:
- Consistent refill accounting across edge/origin so that SSE long-lived sessions and batch callbacks share burst credit predictably according to configured policy.

Relevant logs / headers captured (redacted):
- X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
- X-RateLimit-Reset: 164
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated pool with mixed route weighting: priority lane for SSE, bulk lane for signed-url callbacks.
2) Start ~50 long-lived SSE clients that perform a keepalive ping every 15s.
3) Kick off a batch backfill that issues 1200 callback POSTs distributed over 60s using signed URLs.
4) Observe SSE clients encountering 429s within 10-20 minutes and batch callbacks returning 429 intermittently even when console shows burst credits.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Ava Martinez (Support): Filed after replication by EdgeScale CS. Requested request_id samples and ingress logs.
2026-03-12 - EdgeScale Labs (Customer): Provided request_ids: req_8a7f, req_8a88, req_8b01 and console screenshots. Noted behaviour reproducible in us-west but less frequent in eu-west.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Acknowledged. Assigned to rate-limiter oncall. Asked for diff of recent rate-window config change and timing of deploy.

2026-03-13 - SRE (oncall): Initial hypothesis: edge ingress uses signed-url fast-path that applies a local refill offset and counts probes differently from origin refill. Collecting ingress and origin refill logs for a 30m window.
2026-03-13 - Support (Ava): Requested advice for immediate mitigation: should customer reduce batch callback concurrency or enable smoothing?
investigation_notes: Ingress logs show signed-url callback requests are being token-accounted at the edge with a refill offset of +800ms compared to origin service window (config flag: edge.refill_offset_ms=800).
Origin rate-limiter metrics show synchronous refill at 1s intervals with smoothing disabled for bulk lanes, causing short-term exhaustion when large callback spikes occur.

SSE keepalive traffic contributes to steady drain; because SSE token windows are longer, bursts from batch callbacks push the shared tenant bucket negative at the edge before origin refill reconciles.
Related: observed drift in X-RateLimit-Remaining exposed on console; console queries are served from origin cache and lag edge accounting by ~60-120s in heavy load.
Checked linked issue SUP-314888 for similar refill-offset discussion; that ticket recommended a config to unify refill offsets across edge/origin for signed-url fast-paths.
proposed_next_steps: Short-term mitigation: advise customer to reduce batch callback concurrency to 10-20% of current during peak and enable client-side exponential backoff for callback retries.
Medium-term: enable smoothing on bulk lane to spread refill and avoid immediate exhaustion (config: rate.smoothing.enabled=true for bulk routes).
Long-term: rollout config change to edge services to remove or normalize edge.refill_offset_ms and add telemetry to surface per-route refill deltas in Console.
Run a targeted canary in us-west with reduced edge.refill_offset_ms and smoothing enabled against an isolated dedicated pool.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13 - SRE: Pushed temporary mitigation to customer: decreased batch callback concurrency and enabled smoothing on bulk lane for their dedicated pool. Observed reduced SSE disconnects within 15m during follow-up run.
2026-03-13 - SRE: Opened PR to normalize refill offsets: github.com/redwood-inference/ratelimiter/pull/412 (refs in ticket).
Follow-up: schedule a controlled config rollout to remove edge refill offset and add refill-delta metric. Post-rollout, run the original reproduction to confirm stability.
